ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under FINTRAC for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons and heads of international organizations; mandatory screening against UN Security Council sanctions, Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, and relevant domestic Canadian criminal and anti-terrorism lists; risk-rating at Medium_Risk_Enhanced requires documented source of wealth, source of funds, and ongoing transaction monitoring; screening must cover all direct and indirect owners at the 25% threshold and every authorized signatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, operated by Service Alberta / Government of Alberta (corporate-registry.alberta.ca; filings made through licensed registry agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta statutory corporate and partnership names must be in Latin script in a form searchable in English or French; non-Latin names require a transliteration acceptable to the Registrar; a limited partnership must contain the words 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.'; the name must be distinct from existing Alberta names and must not be confusingly similar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal refusal or name search rejection, the applicant may request reconsideration in writing to the Director of the Alberta Corporate Registry, attaching a fresh NUANS search report, legal argument, and consent letters for any sensitive token; the Registrar is not bound by a previous informal clearance; a further administrative appeal may be brought to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Rules of Court if the decision is arbitrary, and, failing that, a new name reservation with alternative distinctive elements may be resubmitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-agent address is generally acceptable for a limited partnership's registered/address-for-service requirement in Alberta, but it will not satisfy the Canada Border Services Agency bonded warehouse licensing condition requiring a physical, secured depot located within a designated customs free trade zone; the operating premises must be real commercial premises with storage, inventory control, and CBSA access.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85% probability of unannounced CBSA physical inspection or joint inspection with municipal/trade compliance authorities due to the bonded warehouse licence, customs control status, and enhanced AML medium-risk classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; initial capital contributions determined solely by the Limited Partnership Agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the General Partner subscribes to the initial capital contribution of CAD 50,000 for the formation of the Limited Partnership to engage in bonded warehouse operations within the free trade zone; FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Limited Partnership is adopted at [Insert Address], Alberta, Canada; FURTHER RESOLVED that [General Partner Name] is appointed as the sole General Partner with full power to manage the business and affairs of the Limited Partnership; FURTHER RESOLVED that [Authorized Signatory Name] is appointed as the authorized representative for all regulatory filings, contracts, and banking transactions. This resolution establishes the statutory framework, governance structure, and initial officer appointments for the Limited Partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Limited Partnership Agreement in writing specifying partners, capital contributions, management by General Partner, and bonded warehouse operations. Execute by all partners and have notarized where required. Retain original executed copy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit additional documentation or revised agreement to address any registry queries within the prescribed period

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with federal storage facility standards; no wastewater discharge or VOC emissions permitted from bonded warehouse operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from local fire authority, structural load inspections for warehouse facility, and workplace safety clearance under Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal GST/HST and income tax administration (portal: My Business Account at canada.ca; GST/HST NETFILE); Alberta Ministry of Treasury Board and Finance / Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (provincial corporate income tax administered by the CRA under the Alberta Tax Collection Agreement); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for customs and bonded warehouse licensing and export reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the Alberta Limited Partnership with Alberta Corporate Registry (via Registry Agent, REGISTRY system). 2) Apply to the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 (or online); the BN serves as the master identifier for all CRA tax accounts. 3) Open a GST/HST program account (RT) under the BN — mandatory once Canadian taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or over the previous four consecutive calendar quarters; voluntary registration is available for foreign LPs. 4) Open payroll (RP) and import/export (RM) accounts where applicable; register as a customs client with CBSA for bonded warehouse and FTZ export activity. 5) File the partnership information return T5013 and applicable GST/HST returns; non-resident partners bear Part XIII and Part I withholding obligations on partnership allocations and distributions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the Alberta LP is fiscally transparent for income tax (income/loss allocated to partners under ITA s. 96); no LP-level corporate income tax is imposed. For GST/HST the partnership is a distinct 'person' and the registrant of record. Location in an FTZ/bonded depot does not confer an income-tax exemption; it defers customs duty and GST/HST until release into home consumption, but warehousing services are taxable in the ordinary course.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian law does not provide a corporate check-the-box election; partnership tax transparency is statutory. Relevant elections: (i) non-calendar partnership fiscal period election (ITA s. 249.1(7)); (ii) anti-hybrid mismatch compliance filings (ITA Part 6.3, Hybrid Matching Rule and Excess Return Rule — prescribed forms such as CRA RC4650); (iii) GST/HST joint venture election (ETA s. 273(2)) where the depot is operated as a co-venture; (iv) annual GST/HST remittance election for small suppliers under ETA s. 241.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15; Alberta imposes no provincial PST or HST, so the effective headline rate is 5% federal GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — 'small supplier' threshold: mandatory registration under ETA s. 240(1) begins when taxable Canadian supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in aggregate over the previous four consecutive calendar quarters. A non-resident LP that makes only zero-rated supplies is not required to register but may do so voluntarily. Bonded depot storage and logistics services are taxable supplies unless provided to non-resident recipients; once the threshold is crossed registration is compulsory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based pre-clearance mandate exists in Canada. Invoices must satisfy statutory information requirements (registrant name, GST/HST registration number, date of supply, amount, tax rate, and tax amount described in the Input Tax Credit Information Regulations). Electronic filing of GST/HST returns is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies above CAD 1,500,000. The CRA does not operate a pre-authorization repository for e-invoices; B2G e-invoicing is voluntary under the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under ETA Schedule VI, Part V for: (1) goods physically exported by the supplier, including goods removed from the bonded depot/FTZ for direct export — customs duty and GST are deferred under the Customs Act until release into home consumption; (2) services supplied to a non-resident recipient (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7) where the service relates neither to Canadian real property nor to an individual physically present in Canada — bonded storage and logistics services supplied to the non-resident owner of export-destined goods are zero-rated; (3) zero-rated taxable supplies made to non-residents generally. The claim is substantiated by customs export documentation, non-resident status proof, and payment evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canada Customs Coding Form B13A / electronic export declaration filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED/CCS)
Bill of Lading / Sea Waybill / Air Waybill evidencing physical export of the goods from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/financial institution confirmation of export proceeds received in Canada
Customs Cargo Control Document (CCD) / bonded warehouse removal order and CBSA bonded warehouse license number
Commercial invoice, packing list, and contract/purchase order identifying the non-resident recipient of zero-rated services
Non-resident status declaration or certification for the recipient (supporting ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 service zero-rating)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit protocols require that export zero-rating documentation be retained for six years. Missing or false documentation results in reassessment of unremitted GST/HST, disallowance of input tax credits, arrears interest under ETA s. 280, and a civil penalty of up to 50% of the tax for knowingly making a false statement or gross negligence under ETA s. 285.1. Criminal tax evasion under ETA s. 327 carries a fine of up to 200% of the evaded tax and/or imprisonment up to five years on indictment. CBSA administrative monetary penalties (AMPs) apply separately for bonded warehouse recordkeeping and export declaration contraventions; retrospective clawbacks extend to the full reassessment period with compounded daily interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority under the Bank of Canada Act, in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential regulation of deposit-taking institutions, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist financing administration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), SC 2000, c 17.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility; no exchange-control statute exists (the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951), and the Currency Act, RSC 1985, c C-52, establishes the Canadian dollar as legal tender without limiting foreign-currency dealings. A Canadian limited partnership may freely receive foreign capital, hold multi-currency accounts with Schedule I banks, and repatriate profits to non-resident limited partners without Minister of Finance approval. The only fiscal friction on remittances is Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp), on amounts distributed or credited to non-residents that are of a kind payable as dividends, interest, rent, or royalties, subject to reduction under an applicable Canada tax treaty; partnership income that retains its flow-through character is generally not itself subject to Part XIII unless the distribution is a separate source. Bonded-warehouse earnings derived from storage, handling, and ancillary logistics services are ordinary active business income subject to Alberta corporate income tax at the partnership level only if the entity elects to be treated as a corporation; otherwise each partner includes its share, and non-resident partners may be exposed to Canadian branch tax (Part XIV) if the partnership is deemed to carry on business through a permanent establishment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. A bonded warehouse operator in a free trade zone may retain foreign currency receipts indefinitely, either in onshore CAD/USD deposit accounts at a Canadian Schedule I bank or offshore. Obligations are limited to disclosure: (i) a Canadian-resident partner or the partnership (if it is resident for tax purposes) must file Form T1133 (Foreign Income Verification Statement) where the aggregate cost amount of specified foreign property, including foreign-currency bank accounts, exceeds CAD 100,000 at any time in the year; (ii) physical importation/exportation of currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more must be declared to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) on Forms E667/E668; and (iii) cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable by the financial intermediary to FINTRAC. No portion of bonded-depot export receipts need be converted into CAD for customs or balance-of-payments purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with a material legal constraint. Canada does not issue European-style Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licences; foreign digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) that wish to provide Canadian payment accounts must either (i) register as a retail payment service provider with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act, SC 2021, c 23, which became operational on November 1, 2024, and (ii) obtain money-services-business registration with FINTRAC while operating a remittance-transfer business under the PCMLTFA, or otherwise partner with a regulated chartered bank. An unregistered offshore EMI cannot clear through Payments Canada (Lynx or ACSS), cannot hold a dematerialized CAD account in its own name for the LP, and its use would breach the LP's own bank onboarding warranties. Using a registered Canadian PSP as a white-label payment corridor is permissible, but the primary operating and escrow bank accounts must be held at a Schedule I or Schedule II bank to satisfy the bonded-warehouse customs security and lender requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permissible. No statutory rule requires the GP's directors, officers, or authorized signatories to appear physically at a Canadian branch; OSFI Guideline 6 (Customer Due Diligence) permits identity verification through reliable, independently sourced documents and electronic verification tools, supplemented by a live video conference. In practice, for a non-resident-owned Alberta limited partnership, the bank's Financial Crimes Unit will require: (i) an apostilled or notarized copy of the Certificate of Limited Partnership (or Extra-Provincial Limited Partnership Registration issued by Service Alberta); (ii) the full partnership agreement; (iii) a current certificate of incumbency identifying the general partner and any corporate directors; (iv) a fully completed beneficial-ownership certification naming every ultimate natural person holding, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the partnership interests; (v) source-of-funds evidence (six months of bank statements) for each capital contributor; and (vi) CRS/FATCA tax-residence self-certifications for all non-resident partners. A live video or telephonic interview with the managing general partner and one authorized signatory is routine; biometric in-branch identity checks are generally waived where a Canadian corporate record search is clean and the applicant provides notarized identity documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners holding greater than 25% economic interests with an opaque ownership chain, triggering legal-entity identification gaps under FINTRAC's beneficial-ownership verification requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (a) a Canadian legal opinion from a qualified partnership/tax counsel confirming the LP's flow-through status and identifying all natural-person beneficial owners; (b) a FINTRAC-compliant beneficial-ownership schedule using the 25% control threshold; (c) certified copies of each limited-partner subscription agreement and capital-contribution receipt; (d) six months of source-of-funds statements for every capital injection exceeding CAD 50,000; (e) signed CRS-FATCA tax-residence declarations; and (f) a partnership organizational chart showing each intermediate holding entity that is a resident of a recognized FATF jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded-warehouse and free-trade-zone activity flagged for trade-based money laundering (TBML), particularly invoice manipulation, fictitious inventory, or transshipment misdeclaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (a) CBSA Customs Bonded Warehouse licence issued under section 91 of the Customs Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (2nd Supp), evidencing statutory licensing; (b) signed warehouse-storage agreements with third-party clients itemizing custody, insurance, and subordination terms; (c) monthly CBSA Form B3-3 goods accounting schedules and duty-deferral statements; (d) original transport and trade documents (bills of lading, cargo control documents, commercial invoices, packing lists, and HS tariff classifications); (e) a qualified customs-broker engagement letter confirming continuous compliance; and (f) an independent inventory audit report prepared within the prior 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership with no minimum statutory capital requirement flagged as a shell-risk structure lacking economic substance or treasury credibility.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (a) funded capital-call records and audited or review-engagement partnership financial statements demonstrating a capital account of at least CAD 500,000; (b) executed warehouse lease, free-zone concession term sheet, or propulsion to acquire a bonded depot; (c) projected 24-month cash-flow and multi-currency liquidity plan; (d) two professional bank references from the general partner's home-jurisdiction bank; and (e) a general-partner board resolution expressly authorizing the treasury operations, account signatories, and hedging mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hits on capital-source jurisdictions or counterparties, or a politically exposed person (PEP) among non-resident limited partners, causing enhanced due diligence or an OFAC/OSFI hold on deposits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (a) full PEP declarations and recognized-person status disclosure for each partner; (b) transactional chain of title for all inbound funds (wire trail, bank confirmation, and affidavit of source of wealth); (c) legal-certified confirmation that the partnership and each partner are not listed on OFAC, FINTRAC, or UN sanctions lists; (d) evidence of underlying commercial contracts for the bonded-warehouse operation; and (e) an undertaking to provide quarterly transaction monitoring reports and to notify the bank within 48 hours of any material ownership or activity change.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partner capital contributions must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the partner's own foreign bank account or, where funds originate from a corporate GP, an escrow account with a banking reference. Canada has no mandatory FX purpose-code regime, but the MT103 narrative field should unambiguously state 'Capital contribution to Alberta limited partnership - bonded warehouse depot' and identify the partnership's Alberta Registration Number and business counsel reference to avoid OFAC/KYC holds. The receiving Schedule I bank will verify that the transaction is reportable as an international electronic funds transfer (IEFT) when the amount is CAD 10,000 or more, and may require a capital-call notice and partnership resolution for amounts exceeding CAD 250,000. Funds credited to the CAD operational account are immediately convertible to USD or other currencies through the bank's spot desk without central-bank approval. For concurrent inbound flows from multiple limited partners, use separate MT103s per contributor to preserve auditability; commingling of partner capital in a single wire raises beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds ambiguity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For CAD domestic obligations (warehouse rent, utilities, payroll) use Payments Canada's Lynx (real-time gross settlement for high-value payments above CAD 100,000) or the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for batch ACH/EFT payments below the threshold. For foreign-currency trade settlements, the LP must maintain a USD trade account and clear obligations via SWIFT MT103 (single-credit customer transfer) or MT202 (bank-to-bank) with a precise beneficiary bank identifier; no central-bank pre-approval is required. For supplier or client credit support, Canadian Schedule I banks will issue commercial standby or documentary letters of credit under UCP600, with the MT700 issue message generated through the bank's trade-finance module; the beneficiary receives payment only against presentation of compliant documents (commercial invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and customs entry confirmation). For large-value cross-border payments in CAD, the Canadian bank may route through a correspondent with an omnibus account in the receiving jurisdiction, but the legal settlement occurs in Lynx; use MT103 with the partnership's own account number as the originator to preserve clean payment references. All outbound trade disbursements above CAD 10,000 are subject to FINTRAC IEFT reporting, and transfers to high-risk jurisdictions will require the bank's sanctions-screening and transaction-monitoring clearance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter plain-vanilla foreign exchange forwards on CAD/USD and CAD/EUR, transacted with a Schedule I bank under an executed ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex (CSA), purely to hedge the bonded warehouse's receivables and payables currency mismatch.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CAD against currencies without active deliverable markets (e.g., CAD/CNH or CAD/BRL), cash-settled in CAD, provided the underlying exposure arises from trade receivables of the free-trade-zone depot and the transaction is documented under the ISDA/CSA framework.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS or CCS) converting a USD-denominated warehouse-financing liability into CAD fixed-rate exposure, or vice versa, where the partnership's general partner has derivative authorization under the limited-partnership agreement and the swap is collateralized under a standard CSA.

European-style foreign-exchange options (OTC, zero-premium collars) used to cap adverse CAD/USD movements on planned capital-call conversions, subject to the bank's options-lending and suitability assessment and to the condition that no speculative naked option positions are created for a non-financial partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the initial registration; generally due within 30 days after each anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative cancellation of the LP's registration, a 90-day reinstatement window, and loss of limited-liability protection during the cancellation period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal period, due March 31 of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal period, due the last day of the third month after the fiscal period end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may attract a late-filing penalty, the greater of CAD$100 or CAD$25 per partner per month for up to 12 months; partner-level reassessments and gross-negligence penalties may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership / individual with significant control (ISC) confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (included with Annual Return; changes filed on prescribed ISC form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation at the same time as the LP Annual Return; any transfer of limited partnership interests or change in significant control must be reported within 15 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file change notices can subject the LP and each general partner to monetary penalties and administrative strike-off; continued non-compliance is a due-diligence red flag in banking and AML reviews.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Bonded Warehouse Licence annual renewal and inventory reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the licence anniversary date; the annual bonded warehouse inventory return must be submitted in the prescribed CBSA format within 30 days after year-end if a fiscal-year reconciliation is elected.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal or omission of inventory reconciliation may cause suspension or revocation of the bonded-depot licence, immediate customs bond drawdowns, and suspension of duty-deferral privileges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic Alberta Partnership Act audit requirement for a non-distributing limited partnership; a statutory audit becomes compulsory if the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities laws, if its limited partnership agreement or lender covenants require an independent auditor, or if it meets the partnership-level audit threshold under National Instrument 45-106 for sold securities but fails annual disclosure.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for a Canadian reporting issuer or a LP using the public-accounting enterprise framework; otherwise the LP may apply ASPE under the CPA Canada Handbook. Bonded warehouse accrual records must comply with Canada Revenue Agency and CBSA record-keeping requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Conduct an annual register audit as part of the LP annual return. The general partner must confirm that the Register of Limited Partners is current after any transfer of partnership interests, list any individual or entity with significant control (holding 25% or more of the capital or profits, or having de facto control), and file an ISC confirmation with the Alberta Corporate Registry. Changes occurring during the year are recorded in the minute book and filed within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors if a corporate general partner is used

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $600 – $1,200 per year for Alberta registered office/registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $10,000 – $18,000 per year for a medium-risk bonded warehouse LP requiring an independent audit under the partnership agreement or lender covenant

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% + Alberta 8% = 23% combined general corporate rate; LP itself is fiscally transparent (no entity-level CIT) and corporate partners are taxed at this composite headline rate on allocated business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in Canada. Small Business Deduction: 9% federal + 2% Alberta on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporation partners (CRA/ATB administered). Investment Tax Credits (e.g., SR&ED) only for qualifying activities; bonded warehouse/duty deferral in FTZ is a customs cash-flow benefit, not income tax relief. Alberta Health Contribution Levy applies only to employers with large remuneration (CAD 50M+ payroll).
